item.title: Fort Worth’s Quorum Architects Adds Krut Kavathia to Municipal Design Team
item.description: UTA graduate joins Fort Worth firm to support municipal projects, including North Texas water district work.

item.title: Fort Worth-Area Attorney Emma Grotting Carves Niche in High-Stakes Agricultural Law
item.description: A Weatherford-based attorney is quietly becoming a go-to legal hand for ranchers, horse traders, and agricultural businesses navigating increasingly high-dollar deals.

item.title: Fort Worth’s Paslay Group Merges with Unison To Expand National Aviation Consulting Reach
item.description: Paslay Group joins forces with Chicago’s Unison Consulting, combining program management, financial strategy and analytics to expand aviation advisory services nationwide.

item.title: Meet Our March Fort Worthian, Hannah Lacamp Borer
item.description: Turns out telling the story of a local brand with national ambitions is a natural fit for this Fort Worth native.

item.title: Paradoxically, Fort Worth Gets a Second Original ChopShop
item.description: The grab-and-go spot with surprisingly tasty eats opens off Pennsylvania Avenue in city's Near Southside March 25.

item.title: Chuck Norris, Fort Worth's Invincible Texas Ranger, Dies at 86
item.description: The martial artist turned Hollywood icon — and Fort Worth’s most famous fictional lawman — leaves behind a legacy that blurred the line between man and myth.

item.title: TCU School of Medicine Achieves 100% Match Rate as Class of 2026 Lands Competitive Residencies
item.description: All graduates of TCU’s Burnett School of Medicine matched into residency programs nationwide, with placements at leading institutions and across Texas.

item.title: Fort Worth’s Leslie Shields Turned Pandemic Launch Into Thriving Insurance Business
item.description: Spurred by a mentor’s blunt reminder about ownership, Leslie Shields moved quickly to leave contract work behind and open her own agency.

item.title: Dallas Fed: Texas Rental Market Still Reeling From Apartment Oversupply
item.description: A Dallas Fed study finds Texas’ pandemic-era apartment boom has created a lingering oversupply, forcing landlords to cut rents and offer steep concessions as the market slowly rebalances.

item.title: The Salvatore Brothers Get a Wood-Fired Brick Oven and Open Felina
item.description: Alessandro and Alfonso Salvatore follow up their runaway hit of a restaurant, Bocca Osteria Romana, with a new pizza joint in South Main.

item.title: ‘Back to the Future’ Musical Lands at Bass Hall for Fort Worth Run
item.description: "Roads? Where we're going, we don't need roads." The hit stage adaptation of Back to the Future arrives at Fort Worth’s Bass Hall for an eight-performance run, featuring the iconic characters, nostalgia and a DeLorean that still steals the show.

item.title: TCU Lands $10M Gift From Roach Foundation to Boost Research, Student Opportunities
item.description: The Roach Foundation’s $10 million commitment will strengthen Texas Christian University’s research enterprise, support student-focused initiatives, and advance its goal of achieving top-tier R1 status.

item.title: Duchess Launches Wine-Pairing Dinner Series — and Other Food Scene Scoops
item.description: Elsewhere, Heim BBQ kicks off a food truck concept, Smoke & Bone finds a new home, and a foodie staple reopens.

item.title: Hoque Global, Elon Musk Company, Dallas Team Up on Southern Dallas Tunnel Project
item.description: Hoque Global’s $1 billion University Hills development in Southern Dallas was selected by Elon Musk’s The Boring Company for a mile-long tunnel linking to UNT Dallas’ DART station.

item.title: TEA Appoints Board, Superintendent To Guide Fort Worth ISD Overhaul
item.description: State officials finalize leadership transition as Fort Worth ISD moves into next phase of takeover.
